title: The Counteroffer
logline: Weeks after buying an apartment with mold, Robin is offered her childhood dream: anchoring the national news in Canada, with forty-eight hours to decide. Lily goes to war, Marshall's pro and con list turns into a cry, Ted's grand gesture builds her a fake Canada on the roof, and every counteroffer makes Canada more irresistible, while Barney, who insists he doesn't care, is quietly making the only one that works.
coldOpen: Kids, in the spring of 2013, Canada asked for your Aunt Robin back. She had forty-eight hours to decide. Aunt Lily went to war, Uncle Marshall made a list, I made a gesture, and Uncle Barney didn't care.

couch.line: That's his version, Penny. He made me promise to tell it his way. He had it notarized.

guests.name: Colleen Lapointe
guests.role: Head of news at the Dominion Broadcasting Network in Toronto, down in New York to recruit Robin. Relentlessly polite: apologizes before, during and after every ultimatum, counts the deadline down in hours, and answers every objection by cheerfully adding another deeply Canadian perk.

guests.name: Dwayne Szymanski
guests.role: An actor from Hoboken, New Jersey, who plays a Mountie at children's birthday parties and has never been north of Albany. Booming and eager, says 'eh' after everything, gets every Canadian fact wrong with total confidence, and keeps mentioning his second booking of the night.

scenes.summary: Robin announces the offer: anchor the national news in Canada, forty-eight hours to decide, from a network head who texts an apology every hour. The apartment is just an apartment; the mold is named Sandy. Barney doesn't care. Lily declares war on Canada. Robin claims she doesn't even want it; a flashback to Robin Sparkles singing about this exact job says otherwise. Marshall promises a list, Ted a medium gesture with a Mountie. Barney knows the January low in Celsius, leaves for a 'work call' with a 'Please', and leaves a full scotch behind.

beats.line: It started on a Tuesday, when your Aunt Robin walked into MacLaren's with the face she makes when the news is about her.
Okay. Nobody react. I need everyone very calm and very quiet.
Oh my god. You're engaged. You're pregnant. You're pregnant at your own engage—
Canada called.
The whole country? Robin, countries don't call. They issue statements.
The Dominion Broadcasting Network. They want me to anchor the national news.
Robin, that's incredible! Oh no. That's incredible! Oh no.
It's in Toronto. I have forty-eight hours to decide. And the woman who offered it won't stop texting.
Every hour. On the hour. With an apology.
beats.title: Colleen Lapointe

messages.text: Sorry for all the sorrys. Sorry.

beats.line: Forty-eight hours? Robin, you just bought an apartment. You have a thirty-year mortgage.
Ted, it's an apartment, not a marriage. It has mold.
You named the mold!
I named it Sandy. It's gray, it keeps spreading, and it takes credit for my wall.
Congratulations. Don't care. More booth for me.
No. Absolutely not. Nobody leaves this booth. I am declaring war.
On who?
On Canada.
Lily, you can't declare war on Canada.
Watch me. They won't fight back. They'll just keep apologizing until I win.
Guys, relax. It's just a job. I don't even want it that much.
Robin. You've wanted this since you were eleven.
I was a child. Children want ponies.
Your Aunt Robin did not want a pony.
Thank you, Saskatoon! This next one is about my dream job!
Good evening, Canada, here's the news tonight! Sensible blazer, and the lighting's just right!
When I grow up, I'll be the only person in Canada allowed to interrupt hockey!
You wrote a pop song about this exact job.
It went gold. In the Yukon. That's fourteen copies.
Okay. Big decision. And big decisions need one thing.
Scotch.
A pro and con list. Color-coded. Laminated. On her desk by morning.
And I know exactly what I'm going to do.
Ted. No grand gestures.
It's not a grand gesture. It's a medium gesture with a lot of heart. And a Mountie.
Look, go, stay, whatever. Toronto's fine. Average January low, minus ten Celsius. Very livable.
Since when do you know Celsius?
Celsius? Who's Celsius? Is she Canadian? Don't care.
Gotta go. Work call.
What kind of work?
Please.
Robin. He left a full scotch.
He said he doesn't care.
Barney has never left a scotch. Not in a fire drill. Not in an actual fire.

scenes.summary: Colleen Lapointe arrives at the studio in person. Sandy assumes she's there for him; he's the backup, which horrifies Robin on Canada's behalf. Colleen's sweeteners include the right to interrupt hockey, and a mystery agent who answered 'please' got Robin a hot tub. Lily interrupts before Robin can connect the dots and gives Robin the worst reference in history; every bomb, scotch, guns, Robin Sparkles, only makes Canada want her more. Marshall's laminated list turns into tears and lands him a flight to quiz night. Sandy's sign-off settles it: Robin has to take the job, for Canada.

beats.line: The next morning, with thirty-six hours to go, Canada made a house call.
Robin, a Canadian network executive just walked into the building. Try to be gracious when she picks me.
Sandy, she flew down for me.
Then she hasn't seen me in person.
Robin Scherbatsky! Colleen Lapointe, head of news, Dominion Broadcasting. So sorry to barge in! Thirty-six hours!
Sandy Rivers. I'm prepared to hear your offer.
Oh, you're our backup! If Robin says no, the job is yours. Sorry.
Sandy? Reading the national news? To Canada?
Good evening, Canada. Tonight, news from all seven of your provinces.
There are ten, Sandy.
Then it's an even bigger promotion.
Which is why I brought sweeteners. A parking spot with a block heater. A desk with a view of the lake.
And on hockey nights, you get to interrupt the game. For real news only. Sorry.
I'd get to interrupt the hockey.
Oh, and your agent called this morning. Very aggressive. He got you a hot tub.
I don't have an agent.
Well, somebody does. I asked which agency he's with, and he just said, please.
Please? There's only one man in New York who says please like—
Robin! Don't sign anything!
Lily Aldrin. I'm Robin's reference. I have serious concerns.
Colleen, she beat a polygraph last month. Don't believe a word.
Oh, I believe everyone. It's sort of a national problem.
She keeps scotch in the oven. She owns four guns. She once tackled a man for saying aboot.
Oh my gosh. That's our entire demographic.
Fine. She can't skate.
Excuse me? I was a power forward! I broke a boy's collarbone at his own birthday party!
Did she mention she used to be a teen pop star? Named Robin Sparkles?
Lily, that's why we called. Our whole board has the tape. The chairman cries at the key change.
Every bomb I drop makes you more Canadian!
Robin! The list is done!
I laminated it. Then I cried on it. Laminating was the right call.
beats.title: Robin: Stay or Go?
lines: CON: Who eats the corners of my birthday hotdish?
CON: Polar Vortex becomes just Polar

beats.line: Con. Who eats the corners of my birthday hotdish? Nobody wants the corners, Robin. Only you.
Con. Without you, Polar Vortex is just Polar. That's a bear, Robin. I'd just be a bear.
Oh, that's beautiful. I'm so sorry. We'll fly you up for quiz night.
Every Wednesday?
Marshall!
I'm just asking about legroom!
Colleen, if it helps, I've already written my sign-off. Good night, Canada, and God bless America.
I have to take the job. For Canada.

scenes.summary: Ted's medium gesture: New Canada on the roof, with poutine on the grill, Ted in red flannel and a Mountie from Hoboken who gets every fact wrong. Barney's text says 'don't care' twice. Robin's correcting turns into a homesick speech about rinks and apologetic strangers, and she decides to take the job; Barney will drive her to the airport because he's the only one who doesn't care. The Mountie leaves for his next gig: teaching a man in a great suit to apologize like a Canadian. Marshall asks Lily to hold him, tactically.

beats.line: With twenty-four hours left, I made my move. If Robin couldn't live without Canada, I'd bring Canada to her. Budget: four hundred dollars.
Where's Barney?
He texted. Don't care. Busy. Don't care.
Two don't cares, Lily. In one text. That's a cry for help.
Ted, why does the roof smell like gravy?
Robin, you think you have to choose between New York and Canada. You don't. Welcome to New Canada!
Poutine on the grill. A hockey net by the water tower. And straight from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.
Constable Dwayne! Welcome to Canada, eh!
Ted. Where did you get a Mountie.
Kids' party website. He did a bar mitzvah in Paramus. The reviews said, shockingly Canadian.
Heads up, I can only stay an hour, eh. Got a second booking tonight.
Grab a poutine, eh? French fries, ketchup and maple syrup. Our national vegetable.
That's not poutine. That's a crime scene.
Constable, where exactly are you from?
Hoboken. But I've been as far north as Albany. Twice. Once on purpose.
Fun fact, eh? Canadian snow is warmer than ours. Because of the politeness.
Okay, stop! Canada is not eh and syrup and fun facts!
Canada is a rink at six in the morning. It's your breath freezing on your scarf on the walk home.
It's a stranger pushing your car out of a snowbank, then apologizing to you for the snow.
Oh no. She's homesick.
Robin. Did my gesture just make you homesick?
Ted, I've never been this homesick. And I'm standing in Canada.
Eh!
Stop that.
Lily, your war made them want me more. Marshall's list got him a plane ticket. And Ted built me Canada.
I'm taking the job.
Then we're all coming to the airport.
No airport goodbyes. I'll cry, Marshall will cry, and Ted will make a speech.
A short speech.
You've already made slides.
Fourteen.
Barney's driving me. He's the only one who won't make it weird. He doesn't care.
Well, gotta run, eh. Next gig's a guy who's paying me to teach him to apologize like a Canadian.
Who pays to learn that?
Didn't leave a name. Great suit, though. Sorry aboot everything, eh!
Lily. Hold me.
Marshall, I'm still at war.
Then hold me tactically.

scenes.summary: Robin gets into Barney's limo for the airport and finds Colleen in it: Barney is her agent. He's the only one who asked what she'd get instead of what they'd lose. The gang piles in for a proper goodbye: Marshall's one-column list makes her a Minnesota five, Lily keeps a secret, Ted makes his smallest gesture. Robin, who has left every place before it could leave her, turns the limo around and says no. Barney's last counteroffer: she anchors Canada's national news from New York, and Sandy is banned from Canada. Lily accepts Canada's surrender. Future Ted: two years of Canadian news from 57th Street, and twenty-four uncashed checks under a plaque that says Don't care.

beats.line: Hello!
Thanks for the ride. I needed the one person who wouldn't make this weird.
You called the right guy. I am famously, legendarily indifferent.
Hi, Robin! Sorry!
Colleen? Why is the head of Canadian news in Barney's limo?
Your agent offered me a lift to the airport. Wasn't that sweet?
My agent.
Please.
You said you didn't care!
I don't. I'm an agent. Agents don't care. They take ten percent.
He's ruthless. He learned to apologize from a Mountie. He made me cry twice.
You can't out-negotiate a Canadian. They apologize until you give up. So I apologized harder.
Barney. Why?
Because all week, everybody asked what they'd lose if you left. Nobody asked what you'd get.
So I asked. Turns out, a lot. Including a hot tub.
I'll ride up front with Ranjit and give you two a minute. Sorry.
Barney! Your friends are chasing us in a taxi! Should I lose them?
Let them in, Ranjit.
Robin! I told a cabbie, follow that limo! I've waited my whole life to say that!
We're not here to stop you.
We're a little bit here to stop you.
No gestures. We just came to say goodbye properly.
I revised my list. It's one column now.
Pros or cons?
Just Robin. You're a Minnesota five.
Marshall, there's no such thing as a Minnesota five.
There is now. Please don't tell my mother.
I'm still at war with Canada. But I will never tell anyone you cried at Ted's Mountie.
I didn't.
Vault.
Robin, I wanted to make the biggest gesture of my life. But the biggest thing I can do is let you go.
Ted, that's the smallest gesture you've ever made.
I know. It's killing me. The slides are in the cab.
You know what I've done my whole life? Left places before they could leave me. Every school. Every city. Every guy.
Then I bought an apartment with a mold named Sandy. It's the first place I've ever wanted to stay.
Ranjit. Turn around.
Colleen, I'm sorry. The answer is no.
Oh, that's alright! Your agent said you might say that. So he sent one more counteroffer.
Barney?
You anchor the national news of Canada. From a studio in New York.
It's never been done. It's deeply un-Canadian. We said yes. Sorry.
Clause four, the network removes the Sandy from your bathroom. Clause five, Sandy Rivers is banned from Canada.
That one was free. We were relieved.
Told you, Ted. They'd keep apologizing until I won.
Barney. Come here. Thank you.
Careful. You'll wrinkle the agent.
Ranjit, MacLaren's. My agent's buying.
Hello!
Kids, for the next two years, Canada's national news came on every night from a studio on West Fifty-Seventh Street. Canada apologized for the inconvenience.
So Uncle Barney got rich off Aunt Robin.
He never cashed a single check. All twenty-four are framed in his hallway, under a little brass plaque that says, Don't care.
